business_scope.primary_industry_name: Commercial Shipbuilding of Deep-Sea Dry Cargo and Container Vessels

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid. Common law in nine provinces and the three territories; civil law in Quebec for private law matters. Federal corporate law under the Canada Business Corporations Act applies uniformly across Canada.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (2014)
Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA, provisional application; includes investment protection)
Agreement between Canada and the United States of America, the United Mexican States (USMCA/CUSMA/T-MEC)
Canada-China Agreement for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income (1986, as amended)
Convention between Canada and the United States of America with Respect to Taxes on Income and Capital (1980, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, as amended; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, ss 462.31 et seq. and Part XII.2; Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, ss 21.1-21.4 and ss 106-107 (register of individuals with significant control); Significant Control Information Regulations, SOR/2022-229; FINTRAC reporting and record-keeping requirements under PCMLTFA and associated Regulations.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access. The federal register of individuals with significant control is not publicly searchable; access is restricted to prescribed law enforcement and national security authorities, FINTRAC, the Canada Revenue Agency, and other authorized persons. The corporation must maintain the register privately and provide it to shareholders and prescribed bodies in the circumstances defined by the CBCA.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation or equivalent company registration certificate of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or corporate registrar in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; where the issuing state is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, an apostille is sufficient. Canada's accession to the Convention became effective on 11 January 2024. Non-convention jurisdictions require consular legalization by the Canadian embassy or high commission.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Compliance for each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, depending on the source jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association / Bylaws / Constitutional documents of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or original issuing registry; notarized copy acceptable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization as required by the source jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Individual UBO declaration and sworn statement of beneficial ownership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ultimate beneficial owner before a notary public in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, together with certified English or French translation if the original is in a foreign language

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Duly notarized copy of passport or national identity document for each individual director, officer, and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority or notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and, where required, apostille/consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source of funds confirmation for each substantial shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial institution where the shareholder maintains its accounts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature; apostille is required where the bank's home jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney and corporate authorization resolution authorizing the Canadian incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate shareholder's board of directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and Hague Apostille or consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against Global Affairs Canada's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Lists, and domestic regulations made under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act. Banks and FINTRAC reporting entities also screen against OFAC SDN/List of Specially Designated Nationals as a risk-control measure. Politically exposed persons must be identified under the PCMLTFA, using the statutory definition of domestic and foreign PEPs, holding prominent political or judicial office, and immediate family and close associates. Enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, senior-management approval, enhanced ongoing monitoring, and enhanced record-keeping are required where PEP status or heightened sanctions risk is identified.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre, operated by Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressible in letters of the English or French alphabet and Arabic numerals. Non-Latin script names, including Chinese characters, cannot be used as the statutory corporate name but may be used as a translated trade name or extra-provincial name subject to provincial rules. Federal incorporation does not require mandatory bilingual names, but a French-language version may be necessary for registration in Quebec or for use in French-speaking markets. Official-language transliteration is to be provided in accordance with the Canadian transliteration practice for the source language.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: When the Director under the CBCA refuses a proposed name, the applicant may request a reconsideration in writing within 30 days of the refusal, setting out grounds and filing any corrected NUANS name search report and supporting statutory declarations. The Director may reverse or uphold the refusal. A further appeal from the Director's reconsideration decision may be brought by way of judicial review in the Federal Court of Canada under the Federal Courts Act, RSC 1985, c F-7, within 30 days after the reconsideration decision is communicated, unless an extension is granted by the court. NRD is no longer used; the appeal SOP applies to Corporations Canada administrative decisions.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual mail-forwarding address or post office box is not permissible as a federal registered office. The registered office must be a physical street address in a province or territory of Canada and be accessible to the public during normal business hours. A virtual-office arrangement may be accepted only if the service provider supplies a real physical location, a designated person to accept service of process, and professional reception and document-handling facilities. For a commercial shipyard operating as a federal corporation, the better practice is to maintain a substantive operating address at or near the shipyard premises.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk estimate: Low-to-Moderate, approximately 10-20% annual probability of an unannounced verification visit. Federal corporate registry inspections are correspondence-based and rare. Physical on-site inspections are most likely through Canada Revenue Agency audits, provincial workplace safety and environmental authorities, or Transport Canada marine-safety site inspections. Enhanced scrutiny is elevated in the maritime defense and large-vessel construction sector; a credible commercial substance profile should be documented.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, as amended, ss. 5(1) (incorporation), 8 (certificate of incorporation), 40-48 (share rights and issuance), 102-116 (directors and by-laws), 106(3) (officers); Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001, SOR/2001-512
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) - Federal Corporations Directorate
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1 under the Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001), supported by a NUANS Name Search Report
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is mandated under the CBCA at incorporation. The articles may authorize one or more classes of shares with or without par value, and consideration is fixed by the directors. No statutory escrow is imposed at incorporation; escrow accounts are voluntarily established to support Maritime Installment LC payment structures for vessel construction.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: that the subscriptions of the incorporators for the shares set out in the attached subscription schedule are accepted and the corresponding shares are issued upon payment in full of the consideration; that the registered office identified in the Articles of Incorporation is adopted as the Corporation's registered office in the Province of [Province], with [Provider Firm] appointed as registered agent; that the following persons are appointed officers: [Name] as President and Chief Executive Officer, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Treasurer, to serve until successors are duly appointed; and that the corporate minute book, share registers, banking resolutions, and corporate seal be established. DULY PASSED on [Date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and NUANS Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) - online NUANS portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) preliminary name search via the Corporations Canada online portal or an approved service provider. Submit the proposed corporate name for an official NUANS name search report. If a specific name is desired, file a Name Reservation Request (Form 2) to reserve the name for 90 days; alternatively, proceed directly to incorporation with a valid NUANS report.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name (up to three alternatives)
Statutory declaration of name consent (if required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NUANS report identifies confusingly similar names, revise the proposed name or file a Consent Declaration. A failed name search may be re-run within the 90-day validity window once adjustments are made; a reserved name may be extended by filing a new reservation request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Filing of Articles of Incorporation (Form 1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Electronically complete and file Form 1 (Articles of Incorporation), Form 3 (Initial Registered Office Address) and Form 6 (List of First Directors). Verify that the articles include the corporate name, the province of registered office, the share structure (authorized classes, rights, and restrictions), the number of directors, and any permitted restrictions on business. Pay the CAD 200 online filing fee and submit the incorporator's Online Filing Declaration.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report (issued within 90 days)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Corporations Canada issues a Notice of Default for deficient articles, file a corrective amendment together with the required declaration within 30 days. Refusal of electronic filing may be cured by resubmitting in paper form with notarized signatures and payment of the USD-converted fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval of the articles, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation (Form 2), establishing the corporation's existence under section 8 of the CBCA. Download the electronic certificate and record the Federal Business Number, Corporate Access Number (CAN), and Corporation Key for subsequent CRA and registry access.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed, track status through Corporations Canada's online tracker or request a review. Material typing errors in the certificate may be corrected by written request to the Registrar under section 8(2) of the CBCA; substantive changes are made by filing Articles of Amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Organizational Meeting, By-laws Adoption, and Board Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation's directors (internal corporate act; no government filing required at this step except as noted)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first directors' meeting and pass the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution: acceptance of share subscriptions, adoption of the registered office and agent, appointment of officers, banking resolutions, establishment of the minute book and share registers, and adoption of By-Law No. 1 (general operating by-law) under section 116 of the CBCA.
required_dossiers: Officer Appointments and Register of Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Incomplete minutes or resolutions may be ratified by a subsequent written resolution signed by all directors within 30 days and placed in the minute book. Share capital deficiencies are corrected by filing Articles of Amendment or by issuing additional share subscriptions approved by the directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Tax Registration, Provincial Extra-Provincial Licensing, and Banking/Escrow Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); provincial ministry (e.g., ServiceOntario for Ontario extra-provincial registration); chartered bank for escrow and LC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register with the CRA for the corporate Business Number (BN) including GST/HST account (if taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000), payroll account for source deductions, and import/export account for shipbuilding materials and vessel exports. Where the shipyard operates in a province other than the registered office province, register extra-provincially under the relevant provincial Business Corporations Act. Open corporate bank accounts and execute escrow documentation and Maritime Installment LC instruments for construction payments.
required_dossiers: Corporate Access Number and Corporation Key
CRA Form RC1 - Request for a Business Number
Bank account mandate and escrow instructions for Maritime Installment LC
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA registration is queried, use the CRA Business Account Update service or file Form RC101 to correct the BN profile. If extra-provincial registration is rejected, file the corrected application with the provincial registry within 30 days of the deficiency notice and pay any additional fee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Transport Canada - Marine Safety Directorate (in coordination with Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada for industrial policy and Defence/Export controls); provincial occupational health and safety authorities for workplace licensing
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Shipbuilding and Ship Repair Facility Operating Authorization (Marine Safety Compliance Certificate) under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001 and the Marine Machinery Regulations, including Vessel Construction Plan Approval and Safety Management System certification

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) and the Impact Assessment Agency of Canada (IAAC)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Screening-level / Category B environmental assessment under the Impact Assessment Act (IAA), subject to an Environmental Protection Compliance Plan and provincial Environmental Compliance Approval (ECA); a full federal Impact Assessment may be designated for new shipyard construction or major facility expansions.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must be free of deleterious substances under section 36(3) of the Fisheries Act and comply with provincial effluent water quality guidelines; VOC and air emissions from shipbuilding coating and blasting operations must meet Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 (CEPA) emission limits and provincial air quality criteria; hazardous waste handling and disposal must comply with the Cross-Border Movement of Hazardous Waste and Hazardous Recyclable Material Regulations; vessel ballast water management must comply with the Ballast Water Control and Management Regulations under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification per the National Fire Code of Canada issued by the local Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ); structural load inspections and crane certification for shipyard buildings and gantry cranes under the National Building Code of Canada and provincial OHS regulations; workplace clearance/certificate of fitness under the Canada Labour Code Part II and the Canadian Occupational Health and Safety Regulations, including WHMIS 2015, fall protection, confined space entry, and emergency response planning.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), including the Business Registration Online service, My Business Account, and Represent a Client portal. Export and import customs declarations are administered through the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) Assessment and Revenue Management (CARM) client portal. Provincial tax registrations may additionally be required with the relevant provincial revenue authority.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A corporation must obtain a Canada Revenue Agency Business Number (BN) and the applicable program accounts. The applicant submits incorporation documents, registered office and mailing address, directors and authorized representatives, business activities, fiscal year information, ownership and contact details through CRA Business Registration Online, by telephone, or through an authorized representative. A non-resident entity without a Canadian permanent establishment may apply for a BN and, where it carries on taxable activities in Canada or makes specified supplies, a GST/HST program account. The CRA may request certified constitutional documents, proof of identity, authority documentation, Canadian business addresses, contracts, customs records, and information concerning Canadian activities. A GST/HST account is generally required before the first taxable supply after the registration obligation arises. Separate payroll, import-export, excise, and provincial registration accounts may be required. A federal corporation must also maintain its corporate registration with Corporations Canada; corporate registration does not itself create a CRA tax account.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Canadian corporation is generally a separate taxable person subject to federal income tax and applicable provincial or territorial income tax on taxable income. Canada has no United States-style check-the-box regime. A federally incorporated corporation does not automatically receive a federal-only income-tax treatment because provincial or territorial corporate income tax generally depends on the allocation of taxable income and the corporation's permanent establishment or business activities. A non-resident corporation is generally taxable in Canada on income from a Canadian business, income attributable to a Canadian permanent establishment, and specified Canadian-source income, subject to treaty relief. A Canadian-resident corporation is generally taxable on worldwide income, subject to applicable foreign tax relief.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a general check-the-box election to classify an eligible corporation as a partnership or pass-through entity. A corporation may make specific statutory elections where conditions are met, including elections relating to capital dividends, tax-deferred transfers of eligible property under section 85 of the Income Tax Act, amalgamations, wind-ups, foreign affiliates, functional currency, and GST/HST joint ventures or elections. A Canadian unlimited liability corporation may have different classification consequences under certain foreign tax systems, but it remains a corporation under Canadian domestic law and does not constitute a general Canadian pass-through election. Hybrid mismatch outcomes must be analyzed under Canadian anti-hybrid rules, treaty provisions, and the law of the counterparty jurisdiction.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) and Harmonized Sales Tax (HST), administered federally by the Canada Revenue Agency, together with provincial retail sales taxes or provincial sales tax systems where applicable. The federal GST rate is 5%. HST applies in participating provinces at combined rates generally ranging from 13% to 15%, depending on the province. Non-participating provinces may impose separate provincial sales taxes, including British Columbia PST, Saskatchewan PST, Manitoba RST, and Quebec QST administered by Revenu Quebec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies, excluding zero-rated supplies in the relevant small-supplier calculation, generally measured over the applicable single-calendar-quarter and preceding four consecutive calendar-quarter periods. The threshold does not generally apply to certain public service bodies, charities, taxi or commercial ride services, and non-residents making supplies through specified Canadian activities or arrangements. A person carrying on business in Canada may be required to register even where the small-supplier threshold is not exceeded, depending on the nature of its taxable Canadian supplies and applicable non-resident rules. Voluntary registration is generally available, subject to statutory conditions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no general nationwide real-time GST/HST invoice-clearance or electronic tax-invoicing mandate for ordinary business-to-business transactions. Registrants must issue invoices or other prescribed documentation containing required information, retain reliable electronic records, and support input tax credit claims. Electronic invoices are generally acceptable if integrity, authenticity, accessibility, and record-retention requirements are met. No general digital tax stamp is required for GST/HST invoices. Exporters must comply with CBSA export reporting and customs requirements, including the CARM framework and applicable Canadian Export Reporting System procedures. Certain regulated goods, controlled goods, excise products, public-sector arrangements, or provincial regimes may impose additional electronic reporting or documentation requirements. GST/HST registrants generally file periodic returns electronically where required by CRA filing rules and remit tax by the statutory payment deadline.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Qualifying exported goods are generally zero-rated for GST/HST when the goods are supplied for export and the statutory conditions are satisfied, including exportation from Canada in the prescribed circumstances and retention of evidence that the goods left Canada. Commercial shipbuilding supplies require transaction-specific analysis because treatment may differ between domestic construction, delivery or transfer of a vessel, repair or modification services, components, tooling, subcontracted services, and supplies made to non-residents. Certain vessels and supplies used in commercial activities may qualify under specific zero-rating provisions, but non-resident status alone is insufficient. Services may be zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident and the statutory conditions are met, subject to exclusions for services relating to real property situated in Canada, tangible personal property situated in Canada, litigation or dispute matters before Canadian courts or tribunals, and services performed in whole or in part in Canada where a specific exclusion applies. Documentary support should establish customer identity and non-residence, contractual scope, place of supply, vessel location and use, export or delivery facts, customs status, shipping records, and payment trail. Exporters may claim eligible input tax credits and request a net tax refund, but must substantiate the zero-rated output and all related input tax credits.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA export declaration or applicable export reporting record submitted through the prescribed Canadian export-reporting system, where reporting is required
Commercial invoice and sales or shipbuilding contract identifying the supplier, purchaser, goods or services, value, currency, delivery terms, vessel or project reference, and destination
Bill of lading, sea waybill, cargo manifest, delivery receipt, or equivalent carrier documentation evidencing shipment or delivery outside Canada
Proof of export and destination evidence, including customs records from the importing jurisdiction where available

For shipyard construction, repair, or modification: vessel registration or identification records, work orders, completion and delivery certificates, custody-transfer records, shipyard location records, and evidence of the vessel's commercial use
GST/HST invoices and accounting records supporting the zero-rated supply and related input tax credits

Payment and banking records, including remittance evidence where commercially available. An inward remittance certificate is not a standard Canadian statutory document and is not generally required solely to substantiate GST/HST zero-rating
Non-resident customer certification and business records demonstrating the customer's status and the commercial purpose of the supply, where relevant
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada has no general foreign-exchange control regime requiring export proceeds to be repatriated within a prescribed number of days, and no general statutory 180-day repatriation deadline applies. CRA may reassess GST/HST where export conditions are not met, supporting records are inadequate, tax was incorrectly charged or omitted, or input tax credits and refunds were overstated. The reassessment may include the GST/HST otherwise payable, denial or clawback of input tax credits or net tax refunds, arrears interest, and applicable administrative penalties. Gross-negligence penalties may apply where a false statement or omission results from gross negligence; criminal prosecution may apply for tax evasion, fraud, or other offences. False customs declarations may result in CBSA reassessment, seizure, administrative monetary penalties, interest, and prosecution under applicable customs legislation. Records must generally be retained for six years from the end of the relevant year, subject to statutory extensions and specific record-retention rules. Voluntary disclosures may be available before audit or enforcement action if the statutory conditions are satisfied.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), acting with OSFI for chartered bank prudential supervision and FINTRAC for AML/CTF monitoring; no centralized foreign-exchange approval authority exists because Canada operates an open capital account and does not maintain exchange controls on cross-border banking transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible on both current-account and capital-account transactions. There are no exchange-control licenses, no prior approval for foreign-currency invoicing, and no currency-quota restrictions in the federal jurisdiction. Profit and dividend remittances by a CA_FED business corporation are permitted without Bank of Canada approval; the only substantive hurdles are Canadian federal income tax compliance (including Part XIII withholding on dividends paid to non-residents) and the need to evidence the remittance against retained earnings or contributed surplus. Foreign-currency bank accounts in USD, EUR, GBP and other major currencies are routinely maintained without marginal approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no mandatory surrender of export proceeds, no statutory conversion ratio, and no time-limited repatriation window for export receipts. A Canadian commercial shipyard classified under ISIC 3011/NAICS 336611 may retain export receivables in the invoiced foreign currency in Canadian chartered bank accounts or in foreign accounts. The applicable statutory requirements are, instead, reporting-oriented: cross-border monetary reporting for movements above CAD 10,000 under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, and accounting/tax deferral rules under the Income Tax Act for unrealized foreign-exchange gains. There is no regulatory compulsion to convert CAD.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account; Operational / Treasury Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account; Operational / Treasury Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account; Operational / Trade Finance Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as an auxiliary collection/disbursement channel; Low as a primary treasury or escrow custodian. Canada does not recognize the 'Electronic Money Institution' (EMI) licensing category. Offshore digital EMIs (including Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer, or similar) must either register as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) with FINTRAC or operate under a Canadian chartered bank sponsorship to hold CAD-linked balances and route CAD settlement. FedPro and provincial securities laws do not confer deposit-taking status on unlicensed EMIs. For a Medium_Risk_Enhanced shipyard treasury, EMIs may be used only for small-value EPC-stage disbursements; capital calls, LC-backed milestone draws and escrow balances must remain in Schedule I Canadian bank accounts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no statutory requirement for directors to appear physically; however, due to the Medium_Risk_Enhanced maritime-manufacturing classification and possible non-resident shareholding, top-tier Canadian banks typically require at least one director or authorized signatory to complete an in-branch meeting or a live notarized identity attestation. Remote video onboarding (e-KYC with liveness detection) is accepted by RBC, TD and BMO for federally incorporated corporations, but Canadian banks commonly impose supplemental conditions: a Canadian registered office address in Corporations Canada records, a Canadian-resident director on the signing mandate, or a recognized legal entity legalization document for foreign shareholders. For escrow signatories, a physical meeting is generally mandated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident controlling shareholders with no Canadian nexus and a UBO chain ending in a high-risk or FATF-listed jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full UBO structure traced to natural persons, certified passport copies of every UBO, Corporations Canada federal corporate profile (including registered office and director register), source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations, notarized board resolution for account opening, existing EPC shipbuilding contract proving legitimate commercial activity, and references from the sending bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Advance capital injection disproportionate to early-stage shipyard cash flow (red flag for latent money movement or round-tripping).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements, signed share subscription agreement, shareholder-loan term sheet, formal capital call schedule aligned with ISIC 3011 construction milestones, board minutes approving the injection, funds-source attestation, and evidence that the injection will be parked in an intermediary escrow mechanism with staged disbursements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/dual-use exposure in trade financing — high-value marine engines, compressors, navigation systems, or export of a completed deep-sea container vessel to non-OECD buyers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: End-user certificates, commercial vessel classification letter confirming ISIC 3011/NAICS 336611 civilian dry-cargo production, comprehensive HS-code bill of materials, export sales contract with Incoterms, appropriate customs declarations, and a written compliance statement that neither the vessel nor its components are military/dual-use controlled items under Canadian and UN sanctions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: KYC physical-presence default — directors reside outside Canada and cannot produce an apostilled or legalized identification package.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled power of attorney and legalized corporate resolutions under the Hague Apostille Convention, notarized director identification, remote-liveness e-KYC acceptance record, consent of the Canadian registered agent, and a corporate certificate of incumbency confirming the certified signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unanticipated third-party payment flows to subcontractors — towing, classification societies, ship repair partners, and component vendors not pre-identified at account opening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-approved vendor onboarding ledger, executed commercial invoices and service agreements, subcontractor UBO declarations, classification-society engagement letters, and an escrow payment-matching schedule defining conditions precedent for each outbound disbursement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inward equity or subordinated debt should be routed by SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for large clearing) to a CAD or USD treasury account at a Schedule I Canadian bank (preferably RBC, TD, or BMO). The payment narrative must classify the transaction under the Statistics Canada / Bank of Canada International Transactions Reporting System category for 'Canadian corporate capital / equity participation.' The complete compliance routing package must include: share subscription agreement, board resolution for capital issuance, updated Corporations Canada federal corporate profile, share certificates, beneficial-ownership declaration, and, where escrow release is required, an explicit instruction matching the escrow conditions. For CAD-denominated domestic transfers, clearing occurs via Payments Canada's Large Value Transfer System (LVTS); cross-border USD consolidations use the SWIFT network with U.S. correspondent bank Fedwire/CHIPS clearing. A 16-character reference containing the federal corporate registry number should be embedded in every incoming wire.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Production-related supplier payments are executed primarily by SWIFT MT103/MT202 with 16-character corporate registry referencing; high-value shipbuilding components (engines, steel plate, auxiliary systems) are settled through irrevocable commercial documentary letters of credit issued under UCP 600 via MT700, payable at sight against compliant transport documents (bill of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, and HS-accurate customs declarations). CAD-denominated vendor payments clear via LVTS or Real-Time Rail; USD payments clear via U.S. correspondent accounts. The treasury must maintain separate escrow sub-ledgers for EPC milestone draws and conditions-precedent verification. Trade settlements should incorporate Incoterms-based invoicing, and where advance payment guarantees are required, the Canadian bank will issue guarantees under SBLC form (SWIFT MT760).
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD and CAD/EUR vanilla FX forwards (tenors 1–12 months, ISDA/CSA-collateralized)
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) aligning USD/EUR project receivables with CAD-denominated debt service
Deliverable European-style FX options (calls and puts) on CAD/USD, CAD/EUR and CAD/GBP for procurement and bidding-curve exposure

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted as secondary hedging vehicles when a specific counterparty cannot provide physical CAD delivery (not standard, but permissible under Canadian derivatives rules)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under Canada Business Corporations Act (s.263)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each incorporation anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Director's notice of default; failure to file within 90 days leads to Canada Gazette notice and administrative dissolution after further 90 days
5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month for 12 months; penalties for repeated failure; possible prosecution and director liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholder meeting and minutes (mandatory internal corporate action)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 18 months of incorporation and thereafter at least once per calendar year, with no gap exceeding 15 months
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold meeting may be remedied by court order; continued default may support Director's dissolution action

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST annual return if below threshold (for business activities, if quarterly not used)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end for annual filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalty of 5% plus 1% per month; arrears interest on unpaid amounts

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: CBCA: public corporations must appoint an auditor; private corporations may dispense with auditor if all shareholders consent. An audit must be conducted if shareholders holding at least 5% of issued shares request it via written requisition.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; ASPE (Part II of CPA Canada Handbook) for private enterprises; shipyard contractors typically choose ASPE unless public.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: CBCA requires an Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register. The register must be updated within 15 days after any change or annual confirmation of no change; no federal public filing is required, but the register must be accessible for inspection by enforcement authorities.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 25,000 – USD 75,000 for commercial shipyard entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% (federal general corporate income tax rate: 38% basic rate less 10% provincial tax abatement less 13% general rate reduction; combined federal-provincial rate may approximate 26.5% to 31% depending on the province of permanent establishment)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No full statutory tax holiday for commercial shipbuilding at the federal level. Preferential mechanisms available: (1) federal general rate reduction to 15% applies broadly to manufacturing and processing profits, including ocean container vessel construction; (2) Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credit — 35% refundable for Canadian-controlled private corporations and 15% non-refundable for large corporations on eligible naval architecture and ship design research; (3) accelerated capital cost allowance at 50% declining balance for eligible Class 53 manufacturing and processing machinery and equipment in the shipyard; (4) immediate expensing of up to CAD 1,500,000 of eligible Canadian property per taxation year under section 110.4 ITA, available for new shipyard machinery.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (section 150(1) ITA). Mandatory electronic filing through the Canada Revenue Agency NETFILE system or CRA-approved professional tax preparation software; large corporations with gross assets exceeding CAD 1M or gross revenue exceeding CAD 3M are compelled to E-file.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. One T2 return per taxation year (fiscal period normally not exceeding 12 months); quarterly federal income tax instalments are required where federal tax payable exceeds CAD 3,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 filing deadline: within six (6) months after the taxation year-end (e.g., a December 31 year-end must be filed by June 30 of the following year). Balance of federal tax due: within two (2) months after year-end for non-CCPCs and CCPCs not claiming the Small Business Deduction; within three (3) months for eligible CCPCs claiming the Small Business Deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gross maritime revenue from construction, repair, and conversion of deep-sea dry cargo and ocean container vessels, including progress billings under long-term shipbuilding contracts and dry-dock service revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shipbuilder carrying on business through a Canadian permanent establishment reports only gross revenue attributable to the Canadian PE; revenue attributable to foreign headquarters operations is excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Page 2 — Line 40 (Net income before allocations)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile net income after matching steel plate, welding consumables, marine equipment, labour, subcontract dry-dock charges, and capital cost allowance under percentage-of-completion or completed-contract income recognition.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the separate-enterprise principle: allocate direct and indirect costs (supervisory salaries, engineering design licences, dry-dock depreciation) to the Canadian PE on a consistent documented basis; retain full working papers for audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adjustments for discretionary reserves, work-in-progress valuation, capital cost allowance, non-capital and net-capital loss balances applied, and any manufacturing and processing deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A treaty-resident enterprise with no Canadian permanent establishment reports nil taxable income; where a PE exists, compute taxable income exclusively on the PE-attributable profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 1 — Lines 552-556 (Federal rate, abatement, and reduction)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 38% basic federal rate, the 10% provincial abatement, and the 13% general rate reduction for eligible manufacturing and processing income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 10% provincial abatement applies only where the PE income is subject to provincial income tax in a Canadian province; treaty-protected PEs without provincial nexus may lose the abatement, raising the federal effective rate to 25%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 7 / Form T106 (Non-arm's-length transaction disclosure)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose all reportable transactions with non-resident related persons: intercompany hull component sales, design-IP royalty payments, group treasury interest, and management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Form T106 is mandatory where the aggregate value of non-arm's-length transactions with one non-resident related party exceeds CAD 1,000,000 in the taxation year; a Canadian PE of a non-resident files in the same manner. Provide transfer pricing documentation contemporaneously.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under section 162(1) ITA: 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per full month late, capped at 12 months; repeat non-filers (penalty on a return in any of the three preceding years) face 10% plus 2% per month. CRA interest compounds daily on unpaid tax at the prescribed rate. Failure to file Form T106 attracts a penalty of CAD 100 to CAD 2,500 per failure; false statements trigger a gross negligence penalty equal to the greater of CAD 100 and 50% of the misstated tax under section 163.2 ITA.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (Part XIII, sections 212(2) and 215 ITA) on all dividends, including deemed dividends, paid by a Canadian resident corporation to a non-resident shareholder; this is a gross-basis withholding tax collected by the Canadian paying corporation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the beneficial owner must: (1) obtain and deliver a Certificate of Residency (Tax Residency Certificate) issued by the treaty jurisdiction; (2) file Canada Revenue Agency Form NR301 (Claim for Reduced Withholding under an Income Tax Treaty), or Form NR303 for interest or royalties, with the Canadian payor before or at the time of payment; (3) retain a certified copy for CRA audit; (4) claim any refund of over-withholding by filing Form NR7-R within two years. Under the Canada-US treaty the dividend withholding rate is 15% for portfolio investors and 5% for a US corporation that beneficially owns at least 10% of the Canadian paying corporation's voting stock; analogous reductions apply under most Canadian DTAs. Where no valid TRC/NR301 is on file, the payer must withhold the full 25% and is personally exposed to penalties for under-withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties (section 212(1)(d) ITA): statutory withholding 25% on patent, design, know-how, and trademark royalties; DTA-reduced rate commonly 10% (Canada-US treaty and most EU treaties), with certain industrial/commercial royalties exempted in some modern treaties. Interest (section 212(1)(b) ITA): statutory 25%; however, interest paid by a Canadian resident to an arm's-length lender is fully exempt from Part XIII withholding under section 212(3)(b) — effectively 0% for ordinary syndicated maritime bank facilities; treaty rates generally 10% to 15%, and many Canadian DTAs apply 0% to arm's-length interest. Participating (equity-flavoured) interest remains subject to the full 25% statutory withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 — aggregate annual value of non-arm's-length cross-border transactions with any single related non-resident that triggers mandatory Form T106 filing and the expectation of contemporaneous Transfer Pricing Local File / Master File documentation. Country-by-Country reporting applies to multinational groups with consolidated group revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000 (approximately CAD 1.1 billion).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not maintain a standalone Economic Substance Regulations instrument; equivalent discipline is imposed through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (section 245 ITA), the transfer-pricing recharacterization rule (section 247(2) ITA), and common-law sham doctrine. An ocean container vessel shipyard must demonstrate genuine operational substance: physical dry docks and gantry cranes, production manpower, real procurement and invoicing flows, and board management in Canada. A nominal Canadian shell corporation used to route hull fabrication profits to a tax-haven parent while lacking operational substance is vulnerable to GAAR disallowance, sham recharacterization, and reassessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly making false statements or omissions in a T2 return, concealing billings on ocean-going container vessel sales, destroying books and records, or maintaining dual invoicing systems for shipyard turnover.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Indictable offence under section 239(1) ITA: fine between 50% and 200% of the tax evaded plus imprisonment up to five (5) years; summary conviction: fine of 50% to 100% plus imprisonment up to two (2) years. The evaded tax is reassessed with daily compounding interest and a section 163.2 gross negligence penalty of 50% of the understatement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who directed, consented to, or acquiesced in the evasion are criminally prosecutable as principals; the CRA may pierce the corporate veil, assess directors personally for unremitted taxes under section 227.1 ITA, garnish personal assets, and obtain court-ordered travel bans and passport restrictions pending collection of CAD 25,000+ federal tax debts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Making a false statement or knowingly omitting a material fact on a T2, Form T106, or NR301 filing, including wilful blindness to diversion of hull fabrication revenue into a zero-rate offshore entity without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Section 163.2 ITA penalty equal to the greater of CAD 100 and 50% of the understated tax for the false statement, plus reassessment of tax, interest, and potential 100% penalty for third-party misrepresentations; a shipping contract auditor or tax preparer who counsels the misstatement faces separate third-party penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil does not shield directors who signed or caused false returns; personal gross negligence penalties may be imposed directly on the signatory directors, and the CRA may seek civil restitution against directors for amounts the corporation cannot satisfy.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Cross-border intercompany pricing outside arm's length — e.g., low-priced hull component sales to a related foreign engine supplier, excessive royalty charges for vessel design IP, or interest-free group loans — combined with failure to prepare contemporaneous Canadian transfer pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Subsection 247(3) ITA penalty equal to 10% of the net transfer-pricing adjustment where the adjustment exceeds prescribed thresholds and documentation obligations are unmet; the full adjustment is added to taxable income with daily compounded interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatically criminally liable, but they may be held personally liable for the unpaid corporate tax debt if the shipyard is stripped of assets; deliberate mispricing with intent to deceive exposes directors to fraud-based civil claims and CRA collection through the corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Laundering large maritime installment payments through layered escrow accounts, shell intermediaries, or falsified supplier invoices to conceal proceeds of unlawful activity; failure to register with FINTRAC, keep compliance records, or report suspicious transactions related to vessel sales.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal Code section 462.31: imprisonment up to fourteen (14) years for laundering the proceeds of crime; PCMLTFA administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 500,000 for a first violation and up to CAD 1,000,000 for a second; the vessel and related proceeds are subject to seizure, forfeiture, and criminal restraint orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners who knowingly direct laundering schemes face individual criminal liability up to 14 years' imprisonment; FINTRAC assesses responsible individuals personally, and courts may impose travel bans, asset freezes, and personal financial penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registering a federal business corporation that is a pure booking shell — no real dry dock, no labour force, no Canadian management — and using it to strip Canadian shipyard profits into a non-resident parent, thereby avoiding the 25% Part XIII dividend withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR disallowance of the entire tax benefit under section 245(2) ITA, plus a statutory penalty of 10% of the disallowed benefit under subsection 245(4) where the taxpayer fails to establish reasonable acceptance; general sham doctrine permits the CRA to treat the transaction as a nullity for tax purposes, reassessing the real economic owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Canadian courts will pierce the corporate veil where the corporation is a sham or an agency of the foreign parent; directors and shadow directors are personally liable for abetting the scheme, subject to civil restitution, director liability assessments under section 227.1, and possible prosecution for counselling tax evasion.
